# www.obico.io

The Obico website — blog, docs, and marketing pages.

## Project Structure

```
www.obico.io/
├── blog/                        # ✅ SOURCE OF TRUTH for blog posts (git-tracked)
├── docusaurus-i18n/             # ✅ SOURCE OF TRUTH for translations (git-tracked)
├── obico-server/                # Git submodule (TheSpaghettiDetective/obico-server)
│   └── website/                 # Docusaurus 3.7 project
│       ├── blog/                # ⚠️  TRANSIENT COPY — wiped on every release
│       ├── i18n/                # ⚠️  TRANSIENT COPY — wiped on every release
│       ├── docs/                # Documentation pages
│       ├── src/                 # Custom React pages & CSS
│       ├── docusaurus.config.js
│       └── build/               # Build output
├── www/                         # Legacy static site (gulp-based)
│   ├── robots.txt
│   └── sitemap-www.xml
├── public/                      # Final merged output (Docusaurus + legacy)
├── release.sh                   # Build & deploy script
├── fix-locale-canonicals.py     # Post-build: fixes canonical URLs for locale pages
├── append_translation_footer.py # Pre-build: adds translation footer to i18n copies
├── translate_blogs.py           # Translates blog posts via Google Translate API
├── SEO-PLAN.md                  # SEO improvement plan & tracking
└── octoprint_plugin_lists/      # OctoPrint plugin listing data
```

### Key Rule: Edit `blog/`, NOT `obico-server/website/blog/`

The Docusaurus blog directory (`obico-server/website/blog/`) is a **transient copy**. It gets wiped and rebuilt from the top-level `blog/` directory on every release. Always edit files in `blog/` at the repo root.

Same applies to translations: edit `docusaurus-i18n/`, not `obico-server/website/i18n/`.

## Development

### Local Build (for testing)

```bash
# Copy source files into Docusaurus project (mimics release.sh)
cd obico-server/website
rm -f blog/* && cp ../../blog/* blog/
rm -rf i18n/* && cp -r ../../docusaurus-i18n/* i18n/

# Build
npm install && npm run build
```

### Dev Server

```bash
cd obico-server/website
npm start
```

Note: The dev server only serves the default locale. For full i18n testing, use `npm run build` + `npm run serve`.

It's the same animation as the JusPrin splash screen: the cone stays still while the name prints one layer at a time. The GIF is recorded at about 8 frames a second, so it looks choppier than it does in a browser.

The concerns I checked, and why none of them stops it:
- **Browser support:** the animation is an animated WebP image, and every current browser plays those, including Safari.
- **Page weight:** the animated name is 72 KB, which is less than many of the blog's post images.
- **People who find motion distracting:** if someone's computer is set to "reduce motion", the box shows a still JusPrin name instead. I tested that setting too and sent a screenshot of the still version.
- **Distraction while reading:** the animation keeps looping beside the article text. That's a matter of taste, not a technical problem. If it bothers you, I can make it play once and stop. The app's About window already has a play-once version of the same file.

On the page, the box is built from separate pieces instead of one flat image. The dark purple background is CSS, the cone is the white JusPrin mark, and the name under it is the animated file from the app. All three image files come unchanged from the JusPrin repository. content.text:
www.obico.io is published. All three spots now promote JusPrin 2 on the live site, and I sent screenshots of the live blog page and home page.

**Commits, both pushed to master:**
- **obico-server**, commit `03aadb13`: the top bar on every blog and docs page, and the blog sidebar box with the animated logo.
- **www.obico.io**, commit `9a2e4c2`: the floating pill on the home page and the Nozzle Ninja page.

**What I checked on the live site after clearing the CloudFront cache:**
- The home page and the Nozzle Ninja page show the new pill.
- The blog list, an older post and the German blog list show the new top bar and sidebar box.
- The old failure-detection ad appears on none of them.
- The animated name image loads.

**Why I didn't use the release script as-is:** `release.sh` built everything, then stopped before uploading. Its `git pull` refused to run because www.obico.io had uncommitted changes. One of them isn't mine: while the release was running, another session added this paragraph to the JusPrin privacy policy page (`www/src/jusprin-privacy.html`): "That the app started: each time you open JusPrin, it tells us its version, your operating system, and a random id…". A privacy-policy change shouldn't go live unreviewed, so I finished the release by hand. I built those pages from a clean copy of the committed code, then did the upload and cache clear the way the script does. The live privacy page doesn't have that paragraph. The edit is still uncommitted in your checkout, untouched.

**Left as is in www.obico.io:**
- That privacy-policy edit.
- The obico-server submodule pointer, which your rules say I must not commit.
